MINUTES

  ADJOURNED

  CITY COUNCIL

  MEETING

  APRIL 12, 2016

An adjourned meeting of the City Council of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order at
6:13 p.m. in the City Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by MAYOR
ZUCKERMAN.

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
City Council Member Absent:  Schmitz

City Staff Present:  City Manager Doug Prichard
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis

2.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  REVIEW OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES RESERVE FUND POLICY

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve conceptual changes to fund
  balance exhibit assignments.

  City Manager Prichard noted that the need for a financial consultant was raised at
  the First Quarter Budget Study Session in response to the recently identified
  PERS Unfunded Accrued Liability (UAL). He further noted that the Council
  subcommittee and staff selected KNN to provide thorough analysis of competing
  financial needs, with the first step being review of the City’s fund balances and
  policies.

  Mark Young, Managing Director, KNN Public Finance, provided an overview of his
  firm. He reported that the City reserves according to the Government Finance
  Officers Association (GFOA) are standard and that the subcommittee and staff
  reviewed the analysis with a few minor changes.

  Mr. Young reported on the following results of the analysis:

  Vulnerability to Extreme Events – MAYOR ZUCKERMAN noted that discussion
  took place with the subcommittee regarding potential landslide issues on Deep
  Valley Drive and wildfire hazard zones.

  Revenue Source Stability – Mr. Young reported that there is significant fluctuation
  in building permits depending on development activity, and that sales tax is also
  subject to fluctuations with the economy. MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted
  that sales tax should increase due to new businesses coming into the City.

  Expenditure Volatility – City Manager Prichard noted that this is more related to
  capital expenditures, as operating expenditures are very stable.

  Leverage – Mr. Young reported that the City has virtually no debt.

  Liquidity – It was reported that the City is waiting for reimbursements from the
  state and county for general funds spent on various projects.

ADJOURNED
CITY COUNCIL
MINUTES
APRIL 12, 2016
   Other Funds Dependency – Mr. Young reported that the City is in better shape
  than most cities in terms of the need for general funds to support enterprises.

  Growth – Mr. Young reported that commercial growth is generally positive for
  revenue, but that with residential development comes the need for services.

  Capital Projects – Mr. Young reported that street maintenance, storm drains, etc.,
  have been identified as a high priority.

  Recommended Reserve Policy – Mr. Young noted that although total risks to the
  City are low to moderate, he suggested a higher reserve target than the GFOA
  minimum of two months’ operating expenditures. He further noted that the
  COUNCIL should formalize a policy whereby an emergency reserve is set at
  $1,200,000 and a contingency reserve is set at an amount such that when
  combined, the emergency and contingency reserves equal 25% of the City’s
  annual operating expenditures.

  Following MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN’S comments regarding next steps, Mr.
  Young stated that with such a policy in place further review will be undertaken
  regarding the competing needs for funds along with options for financing
  infrastructure and other long term obligations such as the UAL. He indicated that
  this analysis should take about six to eight weeks.

  City Manager Prichard noted that a “normalized” budget will be created to identify
  spikes in revenues and plan accordingly.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN noted that now is the opportune time to look at a long-term
  financing plan that goes beyond two years.

  City Manager Prichard noted that unless there is an objection, the FY2016-17
  budget will be created with the recommended reserve policy and further analysis
  will be completed by Mr. Young.

  It was the consensus of the COUNCIL to follow this approach.

3.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 6:50 p.m., MAYOR ZUCKERMAN formally adjourned the City Council meeting
  to the regular meeting of April 12, 2016.

Hope J. Nolan  Douglas R. Prichard
